header: The news card's sources: free feeds the publishers themselves offer. Its first tab is BUSINESS (what the executives of a company read first: The Economic Times, Mint, The Hindu BusinessLine and The Wall Street Journal), then the general headlines in English, Hindi and Bengali. I take headline, publisher, time and link only. A tab shows the feeds that answer; one that fails is left out (and named), and only when none answers is it an error. Business Standard and Financial Express publish RSS feeds, but their servers refuse every automated request (even for robots.txt), so I do NOT use them: I do not work around a feed that cannot be read. The feeds are free to read; some of the stories they point to (WSJ, Mint Premium, ET Prime, a BusinessLine subscriber piece) may ask for a subscription on the publisher's own page, which the card says.

members.name: bn
doc: The Bengali tab is hand-curated (src/lib/live/bengali.ts). I read Anandabazar Patrika's online edition SECTION BY SECTION (each section is a desk), because the paper's own sections are the best judge of what a story is. Its own feed refuses automated requests, so each is a Google News search of that one section (the links lead on to anandabazar.com). The other Bengali papers follow, and help tell what is trending (a story that three papers carry). The Kolkata section lies inside the West Bengal one, so a story in both is filed under the more specific desk (the heavier weight).

symbols.name: PICTURE_REQUIRED
symbols.sig: const PICTURE_REQUIRED = true
doc: THE OWNER'S TWO RULES FOR WHAT A CARD MAY SHOW, WITHOUT EXCEPTION, IN EVERY TAB (the Steel tab and the priority news too). (1) A story with no picture is not shown. (2) A story that needs a subscription is not shown. Both are decided from the story's own page (src/lib/live/pageFacts.ts). The picture is looked for in this order: the feed's own; the paper's own page; a story of the same headline in the picture helpers' feeds; and, for a story still without one, Bing News searched for that very headline (pictureByHeadline), accepted only when an item has the SAME headline, so that the picture is relevant or there is none. No picture after all of that: the story is discarded.

Above the ordinary list stand, from the stories of ALL THREE languages: the deaths of renowned people and the big accidents of West Bengal and India (src/lib/live/priority.ts), each in the tab of the language it ARRIVED in first and in no other (the same news in another language is left out of that tab's ordinary list too). West Bengal first, then India, then (a demise only) the world; the newest first within a scope; at most PRIORITY_CAP. `textsByLang` holds the feeds' texts of the three languages (a missing one is a language whose feeds were not asked, and then its news is not matched). The priority stories of the three languages (before they are assigned to a tab): what buildTab works from, and what the route puts to the judge of sameNews.ts.

The route asks Bing News for each of these headlines (pictureByHeadline) and keeps what it finds in `facts`. A story whose page has not been looked at yet is not here (its page may give the picture), and a paid one is not either.
